rules.quote: Each of 32 independent bits can be written as peripheral outputs in two modes. In the output direction, this module provides direct 32b access to each GPIO value using direct write. This mode allows software to control all GPIO bits simultaneously.
rules.condition: writing GPIO outputs in direct-write mode
rules.statement: Each of the 32 independent GPIO bits can be written as a peripheral output via direct write, giving software simultaneous control of all 32 bits.

rules.quote: Each of 32 independent bits can be written as peripheral outputs in two modes. Alternately, this module provides masked writes to half of the bits at a time, allowing software to affect the output value of a subset of the bits without requiring a read-modify-write. In this mode the user provides a mask of which of the 16 bits are to be modified, along with their new value.
rules.condition: writing GPIO outputs in masked-write mode
rules.statement: Masked write modifies only the selected bits of a 16-bit half, using the user-provided mask and new values, without read-modify-write; unmasked bits keep their output value.

rules.quote: Each of the 32 bits can be read by software as peripheral inputs. In the input direction, software can read the contents of any of the GPIO peripheral inputs.
rules.statement: Software can read each of the 32 GPIO bits as peripheral inputs.

rules.quote: In addition, software can request the detection of an interrupt event for any of the 32 bits in a configurable manner. The choices are positive edge, negative edge or level detection events.
rules.condition: interrupt configured for a GPIO bit
rules.statement: Software can configure interrupt event detection for any of the 32 bits as positive edge, negative edge or level detection.

rules.quote: A noise filter is available through configuration for any of the 32 GPIO inputs. This requires the input to be stable for 16 cycles of the module clock before the input register reflects the change and interrupt generation is evaluated.
rules.condition: noise filter enabled for a GPIO input
rules.statement: The input must be stable for 16 module clock cycles before the input register reflects the change and interrupt generation is evaluated.

rules.quote: Note that if the filter is enabled and the pin is set to output then there will be a corresponding delay in a change in output value being reflected in the input register.
rules.condition: filter enabled and pin set to output
rules.statement: A change in output value is reflected in the input register with a corresponding filter delay.

rules.quote: The GPIO module maintains one 32-bit output register DATA_OUT with two ways to write to it. Direct write access uses DIRECT_OUT, and masked access uses MASKED_OUT_UPPER and MASKED_OUT_LOWER. Direct access provides full write and read access for all 32 bits in one register.
rules.condition: software accesses DATA_OUT via DIRECT_OUT
rules.statement: DIRECT_OUT provides full write and read access to all 32 bits of the DATA_OUT register.

rules.quote: For masked access the bits to modify are given as a mask in the upper 16 bits of the MASKED_OUT_UPPER and MASKED_OUT_LOWER register write, while the data to write is provided in the lower 16 bits of the register write. The hardware updates DATA_OUT with the mask so that the modification is done without software requiring a Read-Modify-Write.
rules.condition: a write to MASKED_OUT_UPPER or MASKED_OUT_LOWER
rules.statement: Upper 16 bits of the write are a mask of bits to modify and lower 16 bits are data; hardware updates only masked DATA_OUT bits without read-modify-write.

rules.quote: Reads of masked registers return the lower/upper 16 bits of the DATA_OUT contents. Zeros are returned in the upper 16 bits (mask field).
rules.condition: a read of a masked output register
rules.statement: Reads return the upper or lower 16 bits of DATA_OUT in the lower 16 bits, with zeros in the upper 16 mask-field bits.

rules.quote: To read what is on the pins, software should read the DATA_IN register.
rules.condition: software needs to read the value on the pins
rules.statement: Software should read the DATA_IN register to read what is on the pins.

rules.quote: The same concept is duplicated for the output enable register DATA_OE. Direct access uses DIRECT_OE, and masked access is available using MASKED_OE_UPPER and MASKED_OE_LOWER.
rules.statement: DATA_OE is accessible directly via DIRECT_OE and with masked access via MASKED_OE_UPPER and MASKED_OE_LOWER, with the same semantics as DATA_OUT.

rules.quote: The output enable is sent to the pad control block to determine if the pad should drive the DATA_OUT value to the associated pin or not.
rules.statement: The output enable is sent to the pad control block to determine whether the pad drives the DATA_OUT value to the pin.

rules.quote: For GPIO outputs that are not used (either not wired to a pin output or not selected for pin multiplexing), the output values are disconnected and have no effect on the GPIO input, regardless of output enable values.
rules.condition: GPIO output is unused (not wired to a pin or not selected for pin multiplexing)
rules.statement: Output values of unused GPIOs are disconnected and have no effect on the GPIO input regardless of output enable values.

rules.quote: Both views alias the same state, and a write to a per-pin register only affects the GPIO it belongs to.
rules.statement: The per-pin and 32-bit register views alias the same state, and a write to a per-pin register affects only its own GPIO.

rules.quote: The per-pin view consists of two separate, aligned address ranges, so access to the data of a GPIO can be granted without access to its configuration: PER_PIN_IO holds one register per GPIO with bit i of DATA_OUT and of DATA_IN. The configuration range holds two registers per GPIO, which directly follow one another: PER_PIN_OE_0 with bit 0 of DATA_OE, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 with bit 0 of the interrupt control and input filter registers, then PER_PIN_OE_1, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_1, and so on.
rules.statement: Per-pin view has separate aligned ranges: PER_PIN_IO holds one register per GPIO for DATA_OUT/DATA_IN bit i; configuration range holds consecutive PER_PIN_OE_n and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_n registers per GPIO.

rules.quote: A register write must cover all bytes of the register that hold a field, so access cannot be granted to only some fields of a register.
rules.condition: writing a per-pin register
rules.statement: A register write must cover all bytes of the register that hold a field.

rules.quote: The output enable and the interrupt configuration of a GPIO are therefore in separate registers, so access to one can be granted without the other.
rules.statement: Output enable and interrupt configuration of a GPIO are in separate registers so access to one can be granted without the other.

rules.quote: The interrupt registers INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST have no per-pin view.
rules.statement: INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST have no per-pin view.

rules.quote: The DATA_IN register returns the contents as seen on the peripheral input, typically from the pads connected to those inputs. The contents of DATA_IN are always readable and reflect the value seen at the chip input pad regardless of the output enable setting from DATA_OE. If the output enable is true (and the GPIO is connected to a chip-level pad), the value read from DATA_IN includes the effect of the peripheral's driven output and will only differ from DATA_OUT if the output driver is unable to switch the pin or during the delay imposed by the input synchronizer and noise filter (if enabled).
rules.statement: DATA_IN is always readable and reflects the value at the chip input pad regardless of DATA_OE.

rules.quote: In the presence of a pin-multiplexing unit, GPIO peripheral inputs that are not connected to a chip input will be tied to a constant zero input.
rules.condition: pin-multiplexing unit present and the peripheral input is not connected to a chip input
rules.statement: GPIO peripheral inputs not connected to a chip input are tied to constant zero.

rules.quote: The GPIO module provides optional independent noise filter control for each of the 32 input signals. Each input can be independently enabled with the CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER (one bit per input). This 16-cycle filter is applied to both the DATA_IN register and the interrupt detection logic.
rules.statement: Each of the 32 inputs can be independently enabled for the 16-cycle noise filter via CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER, applied to both DATA_IN and interrupt detection.

rules.quote: The GPIO controller provides an optional feature to sample GPIO input values as hardware configuration straps. After each reset, on the first cycle when the strap_en_i signal is asserted, the GPIO detects its transition from low to high. One clock cycle later, it samples the GPIO input values and stores them in the HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN register.
rules.condition: after reset, first cycle strap_en_i is asserted
rules.statement: GPIO detects strap_en_i low-to-high and one clock cycle later samples the GPIO inputs into HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN.

rules.quote: Sampling occurs exclusively at this time, and any subsequent changes to the GPIO input configuration will not be captured. This mechanism samples all 32 bits of the GPIO input data, regardless of the GPIO output enable status, providing a reliable snapshot of the input values for firmware access.
rules.condition: after the strap sample is taken
rules.statement: All 32 input bits are sampled regardless of output enable, and later input changes are not captured in HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN.

rules.quote: The GPIO module provides 32 interrupt signals to the main processor. Each interrupt can be independently enabled, tested, and configured.
rules.statement: The GPIO provides 32 interrupt signals, each independently enabled, tested and configured.

rules.quote: Following the standard interrupt guidelines in the Comportability Specification, the 32 bits of the INTR_ENABLE register determines whether the associated inputs are configured to detect interrupt events. If enabled via the various INTR_CTRL_EN registers, their current state can be read in the INTR_STATE register. Note #1: The interrupt can only be triggered by GPIO input.
rules.condition: interrupt enabled via INTR_ENABLE and INTR_CTRL_EN registers
rules.statement: Interrupt state is readable in INTR_STATE only when enabled, and can be triggered only by GPIO input.

rules.quote: Clearing is done by writing a 1 into the associated INTR_STATE bit field.
rules.condition: writing 1 to an INTR_STATE bit
rules.statement: Writing 1 to an INTR_STATE bit clears that interrupt.

rules.quote: For configuration, there are 4 types of interrupts available per bit, controlled with four control registers. INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING configures the associated input for rising-edge detection. Similarly, INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING detects falling edge inputs. INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH and INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW allow the input to be level sensitive interrupts.
rules.statement: Each bit supports rising-edge, falling-edge, level-high and level-low interrupt detection, selected by the corresponding INTR_CTRL_EN register.

rules.quote: In theory an input can be configured to detect both a rising and falling edge, but there is no hardware assistance to indicate which edge caused the output interrupt.
rules.statement: An input may be configured for both rising and falling edge detection, with no hardware indication of which edge caused the interrupt.

rules.quote: Note #2: All inputs are sent through optional noise filtering before being sent into interrupt detection.
rules.statement: All inputs pass through the optional noise filter before interrupt detection.

rules.quote: Note #3: All interrupts to the processor are level interrupts as per the Comportability Specification guidelines. The GPIO module, if configured, converts an edge detection into a level interrupt to the processor core.
rules.condition: edge detection configured
rules.statement: Interrupts to the processor are level interrupts; edge detection is converted into a level interrupt.

rules.quote: Grant each component access to only the per-pin registers of its GPIOs, and keep using the 32-bit registers in software that manages all GPIOs, for example during initialization.
rules.condition: when individual GPIOs belong to different software components
rules.statement: Each component should be granted access only to the per-pin registers of its own GPIOs, while software managing all GPIOs keeps using the 32-bit registers.

rules.quote: PER_PIN_IO_i has fields in bytes 0 and 1, so a write to it must cover both bytes, i.e., be at least 16 bits wide.
rules.condition: when writing PER_PIN_IO_i, which has fields in bytes 0 and 1
rules.statement: A write to PER_PIN_IO_i must cover both bytes 0 and 1, i.e., be at least 16 bits wide.

rules.quote: A byte write returns an error and has no effect, so a capability for PER_PIN_IO_i must cover at least these two bytes.
rules.condition: when a byte write is made to PER_PIN_IO_i
rules.statement: A byte write to PER_PIN_IO_i returns an error and has no effect on the register.

rules.quote: A byte write returns an error and has no effect, so a capability for PER_PIN_IO_i must cover at least these two bytes.
rules.condition: when granting a capability for PER_PIN_IO_i
rules.statement: A capability for PER_PIN_IO_i must cover at least bytes 0 and 1 of the register.

rules.quote: PER_PIN_OE_i and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i also accept byte writes.
rules.statement: PER_PIN_OE_i and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i accept byte writes.

rules.statement: PER_PIN_OE_n and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_n for GPIO[n], n=0..31, must alternate at offsets 0x200 to 0x2fc in 4-byte steps, each 4 bytes long.

rules.quote: Bits: 31:0; Type: rw1c; Reset: 0x0; Name: gpio; Description: raised if any of GPIO pin detects configured interrupt mode
rules.condition: any GPIO pin detects its configured interrupt mode
rules.statement: INTR_STATE.gpio bit is raised when the corresponding GPIO pin detects its configured interrupt mode; the field is rw1c (write 1 clears).

rules.quote: Bits: 31:0; Type: rw; Reset: 0x0; Name: gpio; Description: Enable interrupt when corresponding bit in INTR_STATE.gpio is set.
rules.condition: corresponding bit in INTR_STATE.gpio is set
rules.statement: An interrupt is enabled by INTR_ENABLE.gpio[i] only when INTR_STATE.gpio[i] is set.

rules.quote: Bits: 31:0; Type: wo; Reset: 0x0; Name: gpio; Description: Write 1 to force corresponding bit in INTR_STATE.gpio to 1.
rules.condition: 1 is written to INTR_TEST.gpio[i]
rules.statement: Writing 1 to INTR_TEST.gpio[i] forces INTR_STATE.gpio[i] to 1.

rules.quote: Bits: 31; Type: rw0c; Reset: 0x1; Name: regwen; Description: Write 0 to disable alert testing until the next reset.
rules.condition: 0 is written to ALERT_TEST.regwen
rules.statement: Writing 0 to ALERT_TEST.regwen disables alert testing until the next reset.

rules.quote: Bits: 0; Type: wo; Reset: 0x0; Name: fatal_fault; Description: Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.
rules.condition: 1 is written to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault
rules.statement: Writing 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers one alert event of the fatal_fault kind.

rules.quote: Masked write for DATA_OUT[15:0]. Upper 16 bits of this register are used as mask. Writing lower 16 bits of the register changes DATA_OUT[15:0] value if mask bits are set. Bits: 31:16; Type: wo; Reset: x; Name: mask; Description: Write data mask[15:0]. A value of 1 in mask[i] allows the updating of DATA_OUT[i], 0 <= i <= 15 Bits: 15:0; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: data; Description: Write data value[15:0]. Value to write into DATA_OUT[i], valid in the presence of mask[i]==1
rules.condition: MASKED_OUT_LOWER is written
rules.statement: Upper 16 bits of MASKED_OUT_LOWER are a mask; DATA_OUT[i] for i in 0..15 is updated with data[i] only if mask[i] is 1.

rules.quote: Read-back of this register returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OUT[15:0].
rules.condition: MASKED_OUT_LOWER is read
rules.statement: Reading MASKED_OUT_LOWER returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OUT[15:0].

rules.quote: Masked write for DATA_OUT[31:16]. Upper 16 bits of this register are used as mask. Writing lower 16 bits of the register changes DATA_OUT[31:16] value if mask bits are set. Bits: 31:16; Type: wo; Reset: x; Name: mask; Description: Write data mask[31:16]. A value of 1 in mask[i] allows the updating of DATA_OUT[i], 16 <= i <= 31 Bits: 15:0; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: data; Description: Write data value[31:16]. Value to write into DATA_OUT[i], valid in the presence of mask[i]==1
rules.condition: MASKED_OUT_UPPER is written
rules.statement: Upper 16 bits of MASKED_OUT_UPPER are a mask; DATA_OUT[i] for i in 16..31 is updated from the lower 16 bits only if mask[i] is 1.

rules.quote: Read-back of this register returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OUT[31:16].
rules.condition: MASKED_OUT_UPPER is read
rules.statement: Reading MASKED_OUT_UPPER returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OUT[31:16].

rules.quote: Setting direct_oe[i] to 1 enables output mode for GPIO[i]
rules.condition: direct_oe[i] is set to 1
rules.statement: Setting direct_oe[i] to 1 enables output mode for GPIO[i].

rules.quote: Masked write for DATA_OE[15:0], the register that controls output mode for GPIO pins [15:0]. Upper 16 bits of this register are used as mask. Writing lower 16 bits of the register changes DATA_OE[15:0] value if mask bits are set. Bits: 31:16; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: mask; Description: Write OE mask[15:0]. A value of 1 in mask[i] allows the updating of DATA_OE[i], 0 <= i <= 15 Bits: 15:0; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: data; Description: Write OE value[15:0]. Value to write into DATA_OE[i], valid in the presence of mask[i]==1
rules.condition: MASKED_OE_LOWER is written
rules.statement: Upper 16 bits of MASKED_OE_LOWER are a mask; DATA_OE[i] for i in 0..15 is updated from the lower 16 bits only if mask[i] is 1.

rules.quote: Read-back of this register returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OE[15:0].
rules.condition: MASKED_OE_LOWER is read
rules.statement: Reading MASKED_OE_LOWER returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OE[15:0].

rules.quote: Masked write for DATA_OE[31:16], the register that controls output mode for GPIO pins [31:16]. Upper 16 bits of this register are used as mask. Writing lower 16 bits of the register changes DATA_OE[31:16] value if mask bits are set. Bits: 31:16; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: mask; Description: Write OE mask[31:16]. A value of 1 in mask[i] allows the updating of DATA_OE[i], 16 <= i <= 31 Bits: 15:0; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: data; Description: Write OE value[31:16]. Value to write into DATA_OE[i], valid in the presence of mask[i]==1
rules.condition: MASKED_OE_UPPER is written
rules.statement: Upper 16 bits of MASKED_OE_UPPER are a mask; DATA_OE[i] for i in 16..31 is updated from the lower 16 bits only if mask[i] is 1.

rules.quote: Read-back of this register returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OE[31:16].
rules.condition: MASKED_OE_UPPER is read
rules.statement: Reading MASKED_OE_UPPER returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OE[31:16].

rules.quote: If INTR_ENABLE[i] is true, a value of 1 on INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING[i] enables rising-edge interrupt detection on GPIO[i].
rules.condition: INTR_ENABLE[i] is true and INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING[i] is 1
rules.statement: Rising-edge interrupt detection on GPIO[i] is enabled.

rules.quote: If INTR_ENABLE[i] is true, a value of 1 on INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING[i] enables falling-edge interrupt detection on GPIO[i].
rules.condition: INTR_ENABLE[i] is true and INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING[i] is 1
rules.statement: Falling-edge interrupt detection on GPIO[i] is enabled.

rules.quote: If INTR_ENABLE[i] is true, a value of 1 on INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH[i] enables level high interrupt detection on GPIO[i].
rules.condition: INTR_ENABLE[i] is true and INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH[i] is 1
rules.statement: Level-high interrupt detection on GPIO[i] is enabled.

rules.quote: If INTR_ENABLE[i] is true, a value of 1 on INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW[i] enables level low interrupt detection on GPIO[i].
rules.condition: INTR_ENABLE[i] is true and INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW[i] is 1
rules.statement: Level-low interrupt detection on GPIO[i] is enabled.

rules.quote: If CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[i] is true, a value of input bit [i] must be stable for 16 cycles before transitioning.
rules.condition: CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[i] is true
rules.statement: A value of input bit [i] must be stable for 16 cycles before transitioning.

rules.quote: Indicates whether the data in HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN is valid.
rules.statement: HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID indicates whether the data in HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN is valid.

rules.quote: GPIO input data that was sampled as straps at most once after the block came out of reset. If the parameter is true then GPIO input data is sampled after reset on the first cycle where the strap_en_i input is high. The sampled data is then stored in this register.
rules.condition: GpioAsHwStrapsEn is true
rules.statement: GPIO input data is sampled at most once after reset on the first cycle where strap_en_i is high, and stored in HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN.

rules.quote: If the parameter is false then the register reads as zero.
rules.condition: GpioAsHwStrapsEn is false
rules.statement: HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN reads as zero.

rules.quote: This register aliases bit i of DIRECT_OUT and DATA_IN for GPIO[i]. Bits: 8; Type: ro; Reset: x; Name: data_in; Description: Input data value of GPIO[i], alias of DATA_IN[i]. Bits: 0; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: data_out; Description: Output data value of GPIO[i], alias of DATA_OUT[i].
rules.statement: PER_PIN_IO bit 8 (data_in) aliases DATA_IN[i] and bit 0 (data_out) aliases DATA_OUT[i] for GPIO[i].

rules.quote: Writing it updates only DATA_OUT[i], without affecting the other GPIOs.
rules.condition: PER_PIN_IO is written
rules.statement: Writing PER_PIN_IO updates only DATA_OUT[i], without affecting other GPIOs.

rules.quote: This register aliases bit 0 of DIRECT_OE. Bits: 0; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: oe; Description: Output enable of GPIO[0], alias of DATA_OE[0].
rules.statement: PER_PIN_OE_0 bit 0 aliases bit 0 of DIRECT_OE (DATA_OE[0]).

rules.quote: Writing it updates only DATA_OE[0], without affecting the other GPIOs.
rules.condition: PER_PIN_OE_0 is written
rules.statement: Writing PER_PIN_OE_0 updates only DATA_OE[0], without affecting other GPIOs.

rules.quote: This register aliases bit 0 of INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING, INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING, INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH, INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW and CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER. Bits: 4; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: ctrl_en_input_filter; Description: Input filter enable of GPIO[0], alias of CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[0]. Bits: 3; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: intr_ctrl_en_lvllow; Description: Level-low interrupt enable of GPIO[0], alias of INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW[0]. Bits: 2; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: intr_ctrl_en_lvlhigh; Description: Level-high interrupt enable of GPIO[0], alias of INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH[0]. Bits: 1; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: intr_ctrl_en_falling; Description: Falling-edge interrupt enable of GPIO[0], alias of INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING[0]. Bits: 0; Type: rw; Reset: x; Name: intr_ctrl_en_rising; Description: Rising-edge interrupt enable of GPIO[0], alias of INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING[0].
rules.statement: PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 bits 0..4 alias bit 0 of INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING, FALLING, LVLHIGH, LVLLOW and CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER respectively.

rules.quote: Writing it updates only the configuration of GPIO[0], without affecting the other GPIOs.
rules.condition: PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 is written
rules.statement: Writing PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 updates only the configuration of GPIO[0], without affecting other GPIOs.

rules.quote: It is separate from PER_PIN_OE_0, so access to the output enable and to the interrupt configuration of a GPIO can be controlled independently.
rules.statement: PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 is separate from PER_PIN_OE_0 so access to output enable and interrupt configuration can be controlled independently.

rules.section_title: PER_PIN_OE_1 to PER_PIN_OE_31, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_1 to PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_31
rules.quote: [Note added for NNC Pipeline] These 62 sections of the original document are identical to PER_PIN_OE_0 and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 above, with the GPIO index i (1 to 31) in place of 0: PER_PIN_OE_i aliases bit i of DIRECT_OE at offset 0x200 + 8 * i, and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i aliases bit i of the interrupt control and input filter registers at offset 0x204 + 8 * i (see the Summary table and the Programmer's Guide). Reset default 0x0 and fields as for GPIO[0].
rules.condition: GPIO index i is 1 to 31
rules.statement: PER_PIN_OE_i at 0x200+8*i and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i at 0x204+8*i behave like the index-0 registers for GPIO[i], with reset default 0x0.

rules.quote: Port Name: strap_en; Package::Struct: logic; Type: uni; Act: rcv; Width: 1; Description: The strap enable signal tells gpio to take a snapshot of the input pins. The behaviour of this signal after that event will have no effect.
rules.condition: when strap_en is asserted
rules.statement: On strap_en, gpio must take a snapshot of the input pins and provide the sampled values on sampled_straps.

rules.quote: Port Name: strap_en; Package::Struct: logic; Type: uni; Act: rcv; Width: 1; Description: The strap enable signal tells gpio to take a snapshot of the input pins. The behaviour of this signal after that event will have no effect.
rules.condition: after the strap snapshot event has occurred
rules.statement: The behaviour of strap_en after the snapshot event must have no effect on the sampled strap values.

rules.quote: Port Name: sampled_straps; Package::Struct: gpio_pkg::gpio_straps; Type: uni; Act: req; Width: 1; Description: This vector contains the sampled strap values.
rules.statement: sampled_straps must carry the sampled strap values.

rules.quote: Interrupt Name: gpio[31:0]; Type: Event; Description: raised if any of GPIO pin detects configured interrupt mode
rules.condition: when any GPIO pin detects its configured interrupt mode
rules.statement: The corresponding gpio interrupt event must be raised when a GPIO pin detects the configured interrupt mode.

rules.quote: Alert Name: fatal_fault; Description: This fatal alert is triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected.
rules.condition: when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected
rules.statement: The fatal_fault alert must be triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected.

rules.section_title: ot_gpio_nnc: integration of the OpenTitan gpio for verification
rules.quote: The behaviour of gpio itself is specified only by the OpenTitan documents; this document adds the port mapping, the configurations and what the wrapper does.
rules.statement: The behaviour of the gpio block itself must conform only to the OpenTitan documents; the wrapper must not alter gpio behaviour beyond port mapping, configurations and wrapper functions.

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-002] RACL (register access control) is disabled: every register access is permitted, and no access is rejected for an access-control reason.
rules.condition: RACL is disabled in the configuration
rules.statement: Every register access must be permitted and no access may be rejected for an access-control reason.

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-003] The alert sender of gpio and the alert receiver of the wrapper both use the synchronous clocking scheme (no synchronizer flops on the differential pairs).
rules.statement: The alert sender of gpio and the alert receiver of the wrapper must both use the synchronous clocking scheme, with no synchronizer flops on the differential pairs.

rules.quote: Ping requests are never issued.
rules.statement: Ping requests must never be issued.

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-004] Two design parameters of gpio are parameters of ot_gpio_nnc and are passed through unchanged: Parameter: GpioAsyncOn; Default: 1; Legal values: 0 or 1; Description: "Instantiates 2-flop synchronizers on all GPIO inputs if set to 1." (gpio parameter list)
rules.condition: GpioAsyncOn is 1
rules.statement: GpioAsyncOn is passed through unchanged from ot_gpio_nnc to gpio (legal values 0 or 1, default 1); when 1, 2-flop synchronizers are instantiated on all GPIO inputs.

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-004] Two design parameters of gpio are parameters of ot_gpio_nnc and are passed through unchanged: Parameter: GpioAsHwStrapsEn; Default: 1; Legal values: 0 or 1; Description: "Enable HW straps sampling logic for GPIO inputs at initial cold boot" (gpio parameter list); the behaviour of HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN for each value is given in its register description
rules.condition: GpioAsHwStrapsEn is 1
rules.statement: GpioAsHwStrapsEn is passed through unchanged to gpio (legal values 0 or 1, default 1); when 1, HW straps sampling logic for GPIO inputs is enabled at initial cold boot, and HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN behaves per its register description.

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-005] The verification shall be run in every combination of the two parameters that the run set selects; the default combination (1, 1) is the configuration of the Earl Grey top level.
rules.statement: The verification must be run in every combination of GpioAsyncOn and GpioAsHwStrapsEn that the run set selects; the default (1, 1) is the Earl Grey top-level configuration.

rules.quote: [INT-CLK-001] clk_i is the only clock.
rules.statement: clk_i is the only clock in the design.

rules.quote: All TL-UL and strap inputs are sampled and all outputs change at its rising edge, except for the effect of rst_ni.
rules.statement: TL-UL and strap inputs are sampled and all outputs change only at the rising edge of clk_i, except for the effect of rst_ni.

rules.quote: [INT-CLK-002] With GpioAsyncOn = 1, i_gpio may change at any time relative to clk_i (an input from a pad).
rules.condition: GpioAsyncOn = 1
rules.statement: i_gpio may change at any time relative to clk_i.

rules.quote: With GpioAsyncOn = 0 there is no synchronizer, and the test bench shall change i_gpio only synchronously to clk_i, like the other inputs.
rules.condition: GpioAsyncOn = 0 (no synchronizer)
rules.statement: The test bench must change i_gpio only synchronously to clk_i, like the other inputs.

rules.quote: [INT-RST-001] rst_ni is the active-low reset, asserted asynchronously and released synchronously to clk_i (the reset strategy of the comportability specification).
rules.statement: rst_ni is active-low reset, asserted asynchronously and released synchronously to clk_i.

rules.quote: While rst_ni is 0, every register holds its reset value as given in the register tables of the gpio specification.
rules.condition: rst_ni is 0
rules.statement: While rst_ni is 0, every register holds its reset value given in the gpio specification register tables.

rules.quote: Port: i_a_instr; Direction: input; Width: 1; Meaning: 1: the request is an instruction fetch (a_user.instr_type = MuBi4True); 0: a data access (MuBi4False)
rules.condition: A request is presented on the TL-UL A channel
rules.statement: i_a_instr=1 must make the request an instruction fetch (a_user.instr_type = MuBi4True); i_a_instr=0 must make it a data access (MuBi4False).

rules.quote: Port: i_a_intg_flip; Direction: input; Width: 1; Meaning: 1: the A-channel integrity sent with the request is corrupted (see 4.2)
rules.condition: i_a_intg_flip is 1
rules.statement: When i_a_intg_flip is 1, the A-channel integrity sent with the request must be corrupted.

rules.quote: Port: o_d_intg_err; Direction: output; Width: 1; Meaning: Response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong (see 4.3)
rules.condition: The response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong
rules.statement: o_d_intg_err must indicate when the response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong.

rules.quote: Port: o_alert; Direction: output; Width: 1; Meaning: Alert fatal_fault received (see 5)
rules.condition: Alert fatal_fault is received
rules.statement: o_alert must indicate that alert fatal_fault has been received.

rules.quote: Port: o_alert_integ_fail; Direction: output; Width: 1; Meaning: Signal integrity failure on the alert differential pairs (see 5)
rules.condition: Signal integrity failure occurs on the alert differential pairs
rules.statement: o_alert_integ_fail must indicate a signal integrity failure on the alert differential pairs.

rules.quote: Port: o_gpio; Direction: output; Width: 32; Meaning: GPIO outputs cio_gpio_o: the value of DATA_OUT (see 6)
rules.statement: o_gpio (cio_gpio_o) must carry the value of DATA_OUT.

rules.quote: Port: o_gpio_en; Direction: output; Width: 32; Meaning: GPIO output enables cio_gpio_en_o: the value of DATA_OE (see 6)
rules.statement: o_gpio_en (cio_gpio_en_o) must carry the value of DATA_OE.

rules.quote: [INT-TL-001] The i_a_*, o_a_ready, o_d_* (except o_d_intg_err) and i_d_ready ports are the fields of the same name of the TL-UL device interface tl of gpio, with the meaning given by the TL-UL bus specification.
rules.statement: The i_a_*, o_a_ready, o_d_* (except o_d_intg_err) and i_d_ready ports carry the same-named fields of the gpio TL-UL device interface tl, with TL-UL specification meaning.

rules.quote: [INT-TL-002] a_user.rsvd is 0. a_user.instr_type is MuBi4True when i_a_instr is 1 and MuBi4False when it is 0.
rules.statement: a_user.rsvd is 0.

rules.quote: [INT-TL-002] a_user.rsvd is 0. a_user.instr_type is MuBi4True when i_a_instr is 1 and MuBi4False when it is 0.
rules.statement: a_user.instr_type is MuBi4True when i_a_instr is 1 and MuBi4False when i_a_instr is 0.

rules.quote: [INT-TL-003] The test bench acts as the TL-UL host. It shall follow the host rules of the TL-UL bus specification (for example, the A-channel signals stay stable while a_valid is 1 and a_ready is 0).
rules.condition: test bench acting as TL-UL host
rules.statement: The test bench must follow the TL-UL host rules, for example keeping A-channel signals stable while a_valid is 1 and a_ready is 0.

rules.quote: Requests that the TL-UL specification lists as error cases (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address) are legal stimulus: the device answers them with d_error = 1 as the specifications require.
rules.statement: The test bench may send requests listed as TL-UL error cases (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address) as legal stimulus.

rules.quote: Requests that the TL-UL specification lists as error cases (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address) are legal stimulus: the device answers them with d_error = 1 as the specifications require.
rules.condition: request is a TL-UL error case (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address)
rules.statement: The device answers such error-case requests with d_error = 1.

rules.quote: [INT-INTG-001] The wrapper computes a_user.cmd_intg and a_user.data_intg of every request with OpenTitan's integrity generator for TL-UL hosts (the section Bus Integrity Scheme of the TL-UL bus specification is not written yet; the code is not part of this specification). A request with i_a_intg_flip = 0 therefore always carries correct integrity, and the test bench does not compute integrity itself.
rules.condition: i_a_intg_flip = 0
rules.statement: The wrapper computes correct a_user.cmd_intg and a_user.data_intg for every request, so a request with i_a_intg_flip = 0 carries correct integrity.

rules.quote: [INT-INTG-002] When i_a_intg_flip is 1, bit 0 of a_user.cmd_intg is inverted.
rules.condition: i_a_intg_flip is 1
rules.statement: Bit 0 of a_user.cmd_intg is inverted.

rules.quote: The request then has a command integrity error: a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault in the sense of the gpio Security Alerts table, which triggers the fatal_fault alert (section 5).
rules.condition: request has a command integrity error (i_a_intg_flip is 1)
rules.statement: The command integrity error is treated as a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault and triggers the fatal_fault alert.

rules.quote: [INT-INTG-003] The wrapper checks d_user.rsp_intg of every D-channel beat against the response fields with OpenTitan's response integrity checker for TL-UL hosts. o_d_intg_err is 1 in a cycle where o_d_valid is 1 and this check fails, and 0 otherwise.
rules.statement: o_d_intg_err is 1 in a cycle where o_d_valid is 1 and the d_user.rsp_intg check fails, and 0 otherwise.

rules.quote: A correct device never makes it 1.
rules.statement: A correct device never makes o_d_intg_err 1.

rules.quote: [INT-ALERT-001] gpio has one alert, fatal_fault, sent through an alert sender.
rules.statement: gpio has a single alert, fatal_fault, which is sent through an alert sender.

rules.quote: The wrapper connects it to an alert receiver as described in the alert handler theory of operation (Differential Alert Signaling). o_alert is the alert_o output of that receiver: it is 1 for one clock cycle for each alert handshake that the receiver detects.
rules.condition: For each alert handshake detected by the receiver
rules.statement: o_alert is the alert_o output of the alert receiver and is 1 for exactly one clock cycle for each detected alert handshake.

rules.quote: [INT-ALERT-002] o_alert_integ_fail is the integ_fail_o output of the receiver.
rules.statement: o_alert_integ_fail is the integ_fail_o output of the alert receiver.

rules.quote: A correct sender never makes it 1.
rules.condition: A correct alert sender
rules.statement: A correct alert sender never makes o_alert_integ_fail 1.

rules.quote: [INT-ALERT-003] A fatal alert is repeated until reset (comportability specification, Alerts per Module), so after a bus integrity fault o_alert pulses repeatedly until rst_ni is asserted.
rules.condition: After a bus integrity fault
rules.statement: After a bus integrity fault, the fatal alert is repeated so o_alert pulses repeatedly until rst_ni is asserted.

rules.quote: A write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers one alert event, as the register description says.
rules.condition: A write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault
rules.statement: A write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers exactly one alert event.

rules.quote: [INT-IO-001] i_gpio, o_gpio and o_gpio_en are the peripheral pins cio_gpio_i, cio_gpio_o and cio_gpio_en_o of gpio: bit i belongs to GPIO[i]. o_gpio is DATA_OUT and o_gpio_en is DATA_OE.
rules.statement: i_gpio, o_gpio and o_gpio_en must map to cio_gpio_i, cio_gpio_o and cio_gpio_en_o respectively, with bit i belonging to GPIO[i].

rules.quote: [INT-IO-001] i_gpio, o_gpio and o_gpio_en are the peripheral pins cio_gpio_i, cio_gpio_o and cio_gpio_en_o of gpio: bit i belongs to GPIO[i]. o_gpio is DATA_OUT and o_gpio_en is DATA_OE.
rules.statement: o_gpio carries DATA_OUT and o_gpio_en carries DATA_OE.

rules.quote: [INT-IO-002] There is no pad model and no pin multiplexer in ot_gpio_nnc: i_gpio is driven only by the test bench and does not depend on o_gpio or o_gpio_en.
rules.statement: ot_gpio_nnc must not contain a pad model or pin multiplexer; i_gpio is driven only by the test bench and does not depend on o_gpio or o_gpio_en.

rules.quote: The Programmer's Guide examples assume pads with weak pull-ups connected to the outputs; a test that follows such an example models the pad itself (for example by driving i_gpio[i] = o_gpio[i] where o_gpio_en[i] = 1 and 1 elsewhere).
rules.condition: a test follows a Programmer's Guide example assuming pads with weak pull-ups
rules.statement: The test must model the pad itself, for example driving i_gpio[i] = o_gpio[i] where o_gpio_en[i] = 1 and 1 elsewhere.

rules.quote: [INT-INTR-001] o_intr_gpio[i] is the interrupt output intr_gpio_o[i] of gpio, an event-type interrupt as defined in the comportability specification, with bit i of the registers INTR_ENABLE, INTR_STATE and INTR_TEST.
rules.statement: o_intr_gpio[i] must be the interrupt output intr_gpio_o[i] of gpio, an event-type interrupt per the comportability specification, associated with bit i of INTR_ENABLE, INTR_STATE and INTR_TEST.

rules.quote: ID: D-008; Subject: Strap sampling (GAP-008); Decision: With GpioAsHwStrapsEn = 1, tests keep i_strap_en = 0 while rst_ni = 0 and for at least 4 cycles after release, then raise it once and keep i_gpio constant from 24 cycles before to 8 cycles after that rising edge. rules.quote: ID: D-010; Subject: ALERT_TEST (GAP-010); Decision: Tests that trigger an alert write 0x8000_0001 (regwen kept at 1); the combined write 0x0000_0001 is not used. rules.quote: ID: D-013; Subject: Sub-word and partial writes (GAP-013); Decision: Per the register tool and the Per-Pin Register View text: full-word writes with mask 1111 succeed. A typical use pattern is for initialization and suspend/resume code to use the full access registers to set the output enables and current output values, then switch to masked access for both DATA_OUT and DATA_OE.
In addition to the 32-bit registers, which group the GPIOs by function, the GPIO module provides a second register view that groups them by pin.
This view allows assigning individual GPIOs to different software components, for example to CHERIoT compartments, by granting each component access to only the registers of its GPIOs.

Like the interrupt controller, they are expected to be managed by a trusted software component, for example a trusted CHERIoT compartment, which handles the GPIO interrupts on behalf of the components owning the GPIOs.
The timing for DATA_IN is still not instantaneous if CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER is false as there is still both top-level routing delay and input CDC synchronizer delay involved.
The top-level routing delay depends on the physical layout of the chip.

The input synchronizer adds two flops between the chip input and the DATA_IN register, though the added delay may vary by up to one GPIO clock cycle depending on when cycle each external input transition arrives relative to the GPIO clock.
The strap_en_i signal transition from low to high is expected only once after the reset process.
Initialization of the GPIO module includes the setting up of the interrupt configuration for each GPIO input, as well as the configuration of the required noise filtering.
